notes: The bleached_counter. The circle's living room. Frasier's tombstone is pinned. Sprint 2 ships the tombstone + the W2 readmission moment + two regulars-talking-about-Frasier threads while he's banned. Sprint 3 fills in the rest.

op.body:
Tombstone pinned per the intervention vote. F. is out one week. Standard friendly-ban — no read, no post, no DM through the SNACKS line. The dial rotates Monday.

F. — when you read this on the other side, it's because you read it. Not because I let you. — WM.

replies.body: Seconded. One week. Then he's back at the counter and we don't bring it up again.
Why was the vote 4-1 and not 5-0?
Because he's a friend and one of us thought the friendship outranked the rule. The rule won.

threads.subject: the kitchen line is back at the storefront

op.body:
T. confirmed the kitchen line at Graustark is back up after the spring outage. The number is the number it's always been. The voicemail box is the voicemail box it's always been. The man who answers is the man who's always answered.

Good. — S.

threads.subject: okay but who's checking on him

op.body:
I know it's a week. I know it's a soft ban. But the man is alone in a cathedral office on a Tuesday night with a modem he's not supposed to dial out on. So who's checking on him.

— P.

replies.body: T. is. T. always is. T. checks on him whether we ban him or we don't. The ban is for us. The check-in is what it is.
And JF. JF stopped by the cathedral Sunday on the way back from the lumber yard. Frasier was at the desk reading a book and not the screen. JF said the book was the Pliny. The Pliny is a good sign.

threads.subject: the milestone · the fourteenth fall · Aria

op.body:
Foals. The milestone is the milestone we've all known was coming since the spring. Aria is fourteen. The third has a name now. Nicola has told Frasier the name and Frasier has not told us the name and that is correct.

The family is going to decide Tuesday. The circle is not going to decide for the family. The circle is going to be available to the family when the family decides.

Whatever the family picks, the circle holds the room. The room holds the room. The work is the work.

replies.body: Confirmed. The keel-keeper is at the wheel through the week.
The named hour is longer this week. The room is wider. — P.
Is the room the room or is the room what the room is becoming?

threads.subject: the room upstairs we don't dial much

op.body:
Quiet morning. The arroyo did not run. The bungalow at the bend of the river is on the line for the photo project.

We don't dial the room upstairs much. The room upstairs is the room where the names go. The dial that gets you there is 5550109, which I am writing here because the room upstairs is part of the house and not the basement, and because the rest of you have lost more in the last fifteen years than I have. If you want to read in the room upstairs, dial.

If you don't, the room is fine without you.

— P.

replies.body: Pliny was a good sign. Carry on. — P.

threads.subject: there is a toy synthesizer on the counter now

op.body:
There is a toy synthesizer on the counter now. Plastic, beige, eight big buttons and a shift key. A trucker ate the special, asked if kids ever come in, and left it by the register on his way out. Said the label he orders his games from mails you one free if your letter asks. I didn't ask what that means.

The Hall kid figured out the first eight notes of something on it Tuesday and now every kid that comes in has to have a turn. The batteries are on their third set. Eight notes is apparently enough.

One thing. When the walk-in compressor kicks on, the toy hums along for a second at the tail end of a note. Low. I mentioned it to the repair guy and he said toys do that. The counter has always hummed a little anyway. The toy fits right in. — S.

replies.body: SNACKS that is a PDP Riffmaster and the beige ones go for stupid money to synth people. Do not sell it. Do not let anybody 'borrow' it. The one tone is three oscillators pretending to be one — whoever engineered it was showing off in secret. Keep it exactly where it is. — j.

Batteries by the case at the co-op. Send the invoice to the board.

— W.M.

threads.subject: the high score on the corner table

op.body:
The Galaga table in the corner has had the same high score since before I bought the place. Nobody has beaten it. I have watched three people get close on purpose and pull back on purpose. I asked one of them why. He said it seemed like the man might need it more than he did, wherever he is.

The initials on the score are D.N.D. The kids assume it's a joke about the dice game. It is not a joke. The man was real. He used to come in before my time, played standing up, never sat down, tipped in exact change.

The table stays. — S.

Nicola came through Thursday with Aria, ahead of the weather. Aria took the window seat and the peach pie. She counted the trucks that passed while they ate. Fourteen. She told me the number on the way out like it was change she owed me.

Nicola looks tired. I gave her coffee for the road and did not charge her, and she let me not charge her, which is how you know how tired.

Storm's south of us. Counter's wiped. We're open. — S.
